newsitem.title: UK: BP sees around 10 pct profit growth a year.
newsitem.headline: BP sees around 10 pct profit growth a year.

text.p: British Petroleum Plc said on Thursday that it expects to deliver underlying profit growth at a rate of around 10 percent a year.

BP told shareholders at its annual general meeting (AGM) that it believes it can deliver $300 million through "self-help" in the form of cost cutting and production growth in 1997. It delivered $600 million through this process in 1996.
"In 1997, we expect volume growth, upstream, to continue at the rate set in 1996," said the company in an AGM statement.
"We will have the benefit of the Mobil joint venture in Europe and of the improved quality of our refining portfolio, and our chemicals business will continue to be upgraded."
It said that as a result of these factors it should hit its "millennium" target of $1.5 billion at least a year early.
"This means we now expect to deliver profitable underlying growth at a rate of around 10 percent a year," said BP.
The company said last year that it believed it would be able to add around 50 percent to pretax profits over five years or so from self help - another $1.5 billion.
BP in February reported a big jump in 1996 profit, which climbed by nearly a third to a record 2.62 billion stg.
Chief executive John Browne defended BP's presence in Colombia following claims in the media of links with human rights violations.
After a recent visit to Colombia, Browne told shareholders, "That visit confirmed to me that the allegations made and implied against us are unfounded."
"I believe our presence in Colombia has been strongly beneficial to the local community, and that, despite the difficulties of the situation, our operations have been managed with great care."
Chairman David Simon said a controversial development of Atlantic offshore fields west of the Shetland islands was important to the UK economy.
His comments follow recent protests from Greenpeace, which said the development would have an unacceptable environmental impact.
